clue.text: Size of book needing unspecified amounts cut in a year

indicators.note: cut means a piece is taken away from the longer word for a year

parts.note: a twelvemonth is an old word for a year
nth, as in 'to the nth degree', stands for an unspecified number or amount

explanation.surface: A publisher trims a book's size after a year of indeterminate cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: TWELVEMONTH (a year) with 'cut' removing NTH, the mathematician's unspecified number.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelvemo is the printer's term for a small book format, each sheet folded into twelve leaves.

clue.text: Hit hard in scrap

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed inside the word for scrap

parts.note: to trash something is to scrap or discard it
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone lands a heavy blow during a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit hard' reads as the definition, but only 'Hit' defines; 'hard' supplies H, which goes 'in' the word for scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrash someone is to beat or strike them repeatedly and violently.

clue.text: Painter in back of boat, way down low

indicators.note: down low says, in this down entry, a chunk is shifted to the bottom of the word

parts.note: the stern is the rear part of a boat
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: An artist sits at the rear of a boat, lying low along the way.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the bottom is the end: STERN with ST (way) moved 'down low' to the end gives ERNST.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German-born Surrealist and Dada painter.

clue.text: Native worked on motorway in the BAR country

indicators.note: worked means the letters of the word Native are processed into a new order

parts.note: M stands for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A local labourer toiled on a motorway abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of NATIVE rearranged give VIETNA, then M (motorway) goes on. 'In the BAR' appears to be an OCR garble of the printed clue and is read as linking words.
explanation.definitionFit: Vietnam is a country in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Game of chess, say, overwhelms board leaders

indicators.note: overwhelms here means sits on top of, as one piece stands above the other in a down entry

parts.note: Chess is a stage musical by Tim Rice with music by members of ABBA
the chairs of company boards are their leaders

explanation.surface: A chess game swamps the leaders of the chess board.
explanation.walkthrough: Chess, capitalised away, is the West End musical; MUSICAL placed above CHAIRS (leaders of boards) gives the party game.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical chairs is a party game where players scramble for seats when the music stops.

clue.text: One can't draw very well with it

definitions.text: One can't draw very well with it

parts.words: One can't draw very well with it
parts.note: the surface suggests a poor artist, but draw means draw breath: a respiratory condition makes breathing hard

explanation.surface: Some affliction ruins a person's ability to sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' points to pencils; the sense needed is drawing breath.
explanation.definitionFit: Asthma is a lung condition that narrows the airways, making it hard to breathe in.

clue.text: Rare animal in overturned useless cage in Berlin

indicators.note: in tells us the animal sits inside the turned-over abbreviation
overturned in a down entry means the letters are flipped to read backwards

parts.note: US, short for unserviceable, is slang for useless
the giant panda is a famously rare, endangered animal

explanation.surface: A rare creature is kept in a broken, upturned cage in the German capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'useless' is US as in u/s, unserviceable; 'overturned' turns it round. 'Cage' is the prison sense: Spandau held Nazi war criminals.
explanation.definitionFit: Spandau was the Berlin prison where Nazi war criminals such as Rudolf Hess were held.

clue.text: Heard composer's fragment of music, A part of a cycle

indicators.note: heard means the composer's name is taken by its sound, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: George Frideric Handel was the composer of Messiah
a bar is a short measure or section of music

explanation.surface: A listener catches a snatch of Handel, part of a song cycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycle' suggests a song cycle; it is a bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: The handlebar is the steering bar at the front of a bicycle.

clue.text: Really go off Animal Farm, for example

indicators.note: off means the letters of Really go have gone bad and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A reader complains about going off Orwell's farmyard story.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal 'off' rearranges REALLYGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell's Animal Farm is a famous political allegory, its animals standing for figures of the Russian Revolution.

clue.text: Drink found by smuggler in seconds

indicators.note: found by means one piece is next to the other, here following it

parts.note: a runner, as in gunrunner, smuggles goods
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Alcohol is discovered on a smuggler within moments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seconds' looks like time; it means those who came second.
explanation.definitionFit: The runners-up are those finishing second, just behind the winners.

clue.text: The Al from Paris?

parts.note: read A1 for the printed Al: the top-class expression, rendered in a phrase borrowed from French

explanation.surface: A man called Al hails from the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed Al is A1 misread by OCR; A1 means first-rate, and the French-derived phrase means the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Par excellence, from French, means the best of its kind, just as A1 does.

clue.text: Scrap book's cut-out article

indicators.note: cut-out means a piece is cut out of the yearbook word

parts.note: an annual is a book published yearly
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Scrap the cut-out article from a book.
explanation.walkthrough: ANNUAL with the article A removed leaves ANNUL.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul is to cancel or declare void, i.e. to scrap.

clue.text: Hellish temperature Isaac Newton suffered

indicators.note: suffered means the letters are put through the mill and reordered

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for newton, the unit of force

explanation.surface: Isaac Newton endured a hellish temperature.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange T, ISAAC and N (newton, the unit).
explanation.definitionFit: Satanic means devilish, belonging to Satan and hell.

clue.text: Sign of trouble picking subject for anthem

definitions.meaning: a warning signal that danger lies ahead
The socialist song sung as the Labour Party's anthem

explanation.walkthrough: The Red Flag is the British Labour Party's traditional anthem.
explanation.definitionFit: A red flag is a warning sign, and the socialist banner celebrated in the Labour anthem.

clue.text: Here I must appear in another case: not simple one, say

definitions.text: Here I must appear in another case: not simple one, say

parts.words: Here I must appear in another case: not simple one, say
parts.note: I is the square root of minus one, which features in this mathematical kind of number, as opposed to a simple real one

explanation.surface: Someone must turn up in court for a different, complicated case.
explanation.walkthrough: I is the mathematician's imaginary unit, and 'not simple' gives complex.
explanation.definitionFit: A complex number has a real part and an imaginary part, a multiple of i.

clue.text: In grate etc I hammered a coffin nail

indicators.note: hammered means the words grate etc I are beaten into a new order

explanation.surface: Something was knocked into the fireplace among bits and pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coffin nail' suggests a hammer and nails; it is slang for a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffin nail is old slang for a cigarette, from smoking's deadly effects.

clue.text: What colleagues ideally want to treat worm in wood

indicators.note: in tells us the rearranged letters are placed inside the wood

parts.note: teak is a hard tropical wood

indicators.note: to treat means the letters of worm are processed into a new order

explanation.surface: Workers want to deal with woodworm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to treat' rearranges WORM to MWOR, which goes 'in' TEAK.
explanation.definitionFit: Teamwork is cooperation between colleagues, which every workplace hopes for.

clue.text: Dog's tongue touching me

indicators.note: touching means the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: English is a tongue, i.e. a language
in crosswords, me is the setter of the puzzle

explanation.surface: A dog licks the speaker with its tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Me' is the setter in crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: The English setter is a breed of gundog.

clue.text: Like over the moon when master quits? That's foolish

indicators.note: quits means a piece leaves the longer word

parts.note: over the moon is an idiom, so it is idiomatic
MA is a Master of Arts

explanation.surface: Someone is elated when the boss resigns, which is silly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over the moon' tempts as delight; it is an example of an idiom. IDIOMATIC with MA (master) leaving gives IDIOTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiotic means very stupid or foolish.

clue.text: A pair getting centuries, Essex's first runs: one caught driving culpably

parts.note: a pair is two
C is the abbreviation for century, one hundred, so two centuries are CC

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of Essex is taken

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricket report: two batsmen hit centuries for Essex.
explanation.walkthrough: Twoccer is British slang from TWOC, taking a vehicle without the owner's consent; Essex is an English county side.
explanation.definitionFit: A twoccer is a joyrider charged with taking a car without the owner's consent.

clue.text: Document order given to hairdresser?

definitions.meaning: a document authorising something, such as a licence
a customer telling the stylist to curl their hair might say '...'

explanation.walkthrough: A perm is a chemical curling treatment, so 'perm it' is a request to the hairdresser.
explanation.definitionFit: A permit is an official document granting permission, and it also splits into 'perm it'.

clue.text: In glass, one's dry painting gets very little wear on the exterior

indicators.note: on the exterior means one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: a mini is a very short skirt, very little to wear
painting is art

explanation.surface: A dry painting in a glass case, and a tiny item of clothing outside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the exterior' says the skirt goes round the art. The definition is cryptic: a martini ordered dry, served in a glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin and vermouth, typically ordered dry and served in a glass.

clue.text: Careless end to parade without opening of kit for inspection

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the outer letters go round the inner one

parts.note: loose can mean careless or slack

indicators.note: opening of picks only the first letter of kit
end to picks only the last letter of parade

explanation.surface: A soldier at the end of a parade is lax, with kit unopened for inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' means outside here: LOOSE plus E (end of parade) goes round K (opening of kit).
explanation.definitionFit: A look-see is an informal quick look, an inspection.

clue.text: Dredge up war novel

definitions.meaning: to dig out or gather up from below
Evelyn Waugh's novel about a journalist sent to report on a war in Africa

explanation.walkthrough: Scoop is Evelyn Waugh's satire on war correspondents.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoop is to dig out, and Scoop is Waugh's comic novel about war reporting.

clue.text: Mendelssohn wrote this piece finally on time, in a month

parts.note: Oct is the abbreviation for October, a month

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of piece

explanation.surface: A music note: Mendelssohn finished this piece on time, within a month.
explanation.walkthrough: Mendelssohn's String Octet was written when he was sixteen.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendelssohn's Octet in E flat is a famous piece for eight string players.

clue.text: Post-shock syndrome, out of the blue?

definitions.text: Post-shock syndrome, out of the blue?

parts.words: Post-shock syndrome, out of the blue?
parts.note: a medical-sounding condition after a shock is really the loud bang following a shock wave from a jet in the sky

explanation.surface: Someone suffers a sudden after-effect of trauma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' is a shock wave, and 'the blue' is the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonic boom is the loud bang heard when a supersonic aircraft's shock wave passes.

clue.text: Whinger very taken by sailing vessel

indicators.note: taken by means the abbreviation is received inside the vessel

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing vessel

explanation.surface: A complainer is welcomed aboard a sailing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: V goes inside KETCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A kvetch, from Yiddish, is a person who complains constantly.

clue.text: Feeble elements of PR retracted in misrepresentation

annotationWithheld.why: Feeble elements of PR retracted in misrepresentation (8): R and P go separately into DECEIT, a scattered insertion the grammar cannot express
annotationWithheld.clue: Feeble elements of PR retracted in misrepresentation
